title: Preparing for National Exams
text:
Many students find it difficult to prepare for national exams because the material is spread across several subjects. A common strategy is to create a weekly timetable that divides the syllabus into manageable sections. Teachers often recommend reviewing old papers, since they reveal how questions are usually phrased. Students who practise under timed conditions tend to feel calmer on the actual day.

However, planning alone is not enough. Some learners spend hours rereading their notes without testing themselves, which gives a false sense of confidence. Active recall, such as answering questions from memory, is considerably more effective. Students should also take regular breaks, because concentration fades after long periods of study.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what is a common strategy for preparing for exams?
options: Creating a weekly timetable that divides the syllabus
Memorising the answers to all questions
Studying only the night before the exam

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, why is rereading notes not always effective?
options: It can give a false sense of confidence
It makes learners forget the subject

questions.text: Why do teachers recommend reviewing old exam papers?
options: Because the exam questions are always identical
Because they show how questions are usually worded
Because students can skip the rest of the syllabus
Because they are the only study material allowed

questions.text: What does the passage suggest about students who take regular breaks?
options: They are less likely to lose concentration during long study sessions
They study less than everyone else
They do not need to review their notes
They prefer rereading to active recall

paragraph_translations: Muitos estudantes acham difícil se preparar para os exames nacionais, porque o conteúdo está distribuído por várias disciplinas. Uma estratégia comum é criar um cronograma semanal que divida o conteúdo programático em seções administráveis. Os professores costumam recomendar a revisão de provas antigas, pois elas mostram como as perguntas geralmente são formuladas. Estudantes que praticam sob condições de tempo tendem a se sentir mais tranquilos no dia da prova.

No entanto, apenas planejar não basta. Alguns alunos passam horas relendo suas anotações sem se testar, o que cria uma falsa sensação de confiança. A evocação ativa, como responder perguntas de memória, é consideravelmente mais eficaz. Os estudantes também devem fazer pausas regulares, porque a concentração diminui após longos períodos de estudo.
